exposure: Visceral and parietal peritoneum left open
Three groups based on peritoneal closure status during cesarean section
outcome: Impact of adhesions on reproductive capacity
Pregnancy rate after laparoscopic tubal surgery
cohort: 250 women with secondary infertility after their first cesarean section
finding: Nonclosure of the peritoneum in CS is associated with more adhesion formation, which might adversely affect the future women reproduction.
mod_finding: This study investigated the impact of peritoneal non-closure during cesarean section on adhesion formation and found that non-closure was associated with increased adhesions, potentially impacting future fertility.
